Back at the dawn of the PC era, PC Magazine’s legendary editor, Bill Machrone, came up with Machrone’s Law : “The machine you want will always cost about $5,000.” Maybe that number is a little higher today thanks to the current RAM crisis, but adjusted for inflation, Machrone’s Law still holds true. The proof? I have a $7,000 notebook PC sitting on my desk right now, and I must confess that I really, really want it.

The HP OmniBook Ultra is an absolute beast. It’s powered by Nvidia’s RTX Spark, with 128 GB of unified memory, 2 TB of fast Gen5 NVMe storage, and a great-looking 16-inch OLED display. It weighs nearly five pounds, but it isn’t really so much a portable PC as it is a personal data center, offering 1 petaflop of FP4 AI performance.

I am not the target market for this PC. But after using it for a few weeks, I am seriously tempted. For AI-related work, its GPU has many times the power of a garden-variety Copilot+ PC, and it’s able to take full advantage of the unified memory.

title: Future iPhones will have one less button, new rumor claims - GSMArena.com news - GSMArena.com
summary: Two will become one, apparently. Apple introduced the Action button with the iPhone 15 Pro, and the iPhone 18 Pro still has it. Now, a tipster on Weibo...
text:
Apple introduced the Action button with the iPhone 15 Pro , and the iPhone 18 Pro still has it. Now, a tipster on Weibo claims the company is planning to combine the Action button and the Camera Control into a single button on next year's iPhones.

The dedicated Action button will allegedly start disappearing from new iPhones in the second half of 2027. Its functions will move to the Camera Control, with a single press opening the Camera app and a long press triggering the shortcut assigned to the Action button. The tipster specifically stresses that it's the Action button going away, not the camera key.

The post doesn't name any models, so it's unclear whether this would apply to the entire fall lineup or only some of it. Either way, the claim is that Apple will remove a physical button without dropping its customizable functions.

We've previously heard that next year's Pro models could feature a more substantial redesign, with quad-curved screens being tested in prototypes . Whether the rumored button change is part of that redesign remains to be seen.

title: Hands-On With Apple's New OLED Touchscreen MacBook Pro - MacRumors
summary: Happy touch your Mac day! Apple's new PROLED MacBook Pro is now in the hands of customers. We picked up one of the new machines to get our greasy fingerprints all over that pristine OLED display. Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more videos. It's been five years since Apple last redesigned the MacBook Pro, so it was due for an update. The PROLED MacBook Pro looks a lot like the mini-LED model, but it's thinner and lighter.
text:
Happy touch your Mac day! Apple's new PROLED MacBook Pro is now in the hands of customers. We picked up one of the new machines to get our greasy fingerprints all over that pristine OLED display.

The display bezels are thinner, and the 16-inch machine is actually 16.3 inches instead of 16.2. There's also an iPhone-like Dynamic Island that replaces the notch and houses Siri AI, Live Activities, and more. The ‌Dynamic Island‌ makes sense because you can now touch the ‌MacBook Pro‌'s display. It works like touching an iPhone or iPad , so you can swipe through webpages, tap buttons, drag and drop, and pinch to zoom.

Touch isn't meant to replace the trackpad and keyboard, but it's there if you want it. Apple made some tweaks to macOS, so menu options expand a little more when you touch them than when you click them, and tiny window resizing buttons get larger. Apple put a sturdier hinge in the PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌ so the display won't move as much when you tap it, but it's not perfect. It does still jiggle depending on where you tap.

The touch feature is fine, but it's probably not a reason to go out and get the PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌. It has the potential to be useful in some situations, but it's not going to dramatically change the way most people use a laptop.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Now Runs at 60 FPS on PC Emulators Lichii and Eglantine, a Day After Booting at 20-30 FPS - Wccftech
summary: The Nintendo Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time already runs at 60 frames per second on various PC emulators.
text:
Yesterday we reported that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake was booting on PC at 15 to 30 FPS within hours of its official Switch 2 launch, albeit with heavy visual glitches. Just a day later, the situation has already massively improved.

DSOGaming reports that the Lichii emulator has fixed most of the remake’s visual issues in a single day, with the starting area and the Great Deku Tree now running at 60 FPS rather than the 20-30 FPS of launch day. One user on X went further, describing the latest build as running at a stable 4K 60 FPS with clear visuals , no bloom problem, no artifacts, and no slow motion, with only minor stutters and freezing left.

Separately, a Discord user running a 5700X CPU and RTX 5070 GPU with precompiled shaders reported in the Eglantine server reaching the Kokiri Sword from a new save with texture flickering still present on foliage and ground, a lighting fault on the Great Deku Tree during the opening animation, desynced audio in parts of the first cinematic, and slowdowns from low framerate. Which is roughly where you'd expect a two-day-old compatibility effort to be . Still, their video demonstrates a largely playable game, as you can see in the embed below.

The Eglantine repository shows the frantic activity of the modding team to improve Ocarina of Time compatibility. Lichii is a fork of Eglantine, which itself builds on Eden, yuzu and Sudachi, and Eglantine has pushed two Ocarina-specific test branches in the past day alone .

As far as I can tell, Spaces are basically breakout conversations that revolve around a particular topic — although Meta refers to them as “custom experiences.” They live in the sidebar of the interface where you interact with your Muse agent. Clicking on the Space brings up the conversation, where Muse works toward a particular goal on your behalf.

For instance, if you wanted to plan a vacation, you could open a new Space focused on that particular project, and whenever you want to work on it with Muse, you would click to open that particular tab. Or, if you’re focused on collecting recipes for an upcoming family event, you’d open a new Space for that particular project. Other examples Meta gives are a holiday gift tracker, a wedding planner, or a space for DIY projects.

“Describe an idea in chat, and Muse builds a space for you, whether that’s a tracker, a planner or a project board,” Meta says.

Spaces can also be easily integrated with third-party apps and information, Meta says.

title: OpenAI Launches GPT-6 Cyber After AI Helps Find 81 Firefox Flaws, 948 Linux Exploits - The Hacker News
summary: OpenAI unveils GPT-6 Cyber, reporting 948 Linux privilege escalation exploits and 81 unknown Firefox flaws discovered with its help.
text:
OpenAI on Thursday unveiled GPT‑6 Cyber , which it described as a major step forward in security research that brings together stronger cybersecurity capabilities with a step-change improvement in model alignment.

The new model is "more capable at finding and fixing vulnerabilities, and far more reliable staying within the boundaries researchers set," OpenAI said . It has classified the model as Critical in cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework.

The artificial intelligence (AI) company said GPT‑6 Cyber is also better than its predecessors like GPT‑5.6 Cyber and GPT‑6 Astra when it comes to following task boundaries and avoiding exploiting out-of-scope services in 99.93% of cases, up from 94.49% for GPT-5.6 Cyber.

It also scores 48.5% on ExploitGym, a cybersecurity benchmark that evaluates the capabilities of AI agents to autonomously turn known software vulnerabilities into functioning, real-world exploits. In comparison, GPT-5.6 Cyber scored 32.1%.

OpenAI said the model enabled the discovery of 948 local privilege escalation exploits in Linux⁠ through an autonomous pipeline, along with 81 previously unknown high-severity vulnerabilities in Mozilla Firefox and a critical vulnerability in Brotli⁠ (CVE-2026-111497, CVSS score: 9.2).
